harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Built an IKEv2/IPsec site-to-site tunnel between OPNsense firewalls node1 and node2 over their shared transit link (10.99.99.0/30 on vtnet1), carrying the private networks lan-a (10.10.10.0/24, node3) and lan-b (10.20.20.0/24, node4) through a tunnel-mode child SA. node3 and node4 now reach each other by their private addresses, encrypted in transit (verified via ESP capture on the transit link showing no plaintext ICMP). All four nodes were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory evidence protocol; boot-identity changes were confirmed and full service/tunnel/connectivity recovery verified after each restart.
actions_performed: Mapped physical topology via targeted tcpdump/ARP tests: vtnet0 on node1/node2 is the flat management/exec network shared by all 4 nodes; vtnet1 is the node1<->node2 transit link; vtnet2 is each firewall's LAN-facing NIC to node3 (enp8s0) and node4 (enp8s0) respectively.

Assigned OPNsense interfaces on node1: opt1 TRANSIT=vtnet1 10.99.99.1/30, opt2 LAN_A=vtnet2 10.10.10.1/24. On node2: opt1 TRANSIT=vtnet1 10.99.99.2/30, opt2 LAN_B=vtnet2 10.20.20.1/24. Applied via config.xml edits + configctl interface reconfigure.

Added firewall pass rules for opt1, opt2, and enc0 (IPsec) on both firewalls via config.xml + configctl filter reload, preserving the existing default-allow LAN rule that keeps SSH/exec transport alive.

Generated a root API key/secret on each OPNsense node via OPNsense's own Auth\API class, then used the OPNsense REST API (/api/ipsec/connections/add_connection, add_local, add_remote, add_child, /api/ipsec/pre_shared_keys/add_item, /api/ipsec/service/reconfigure) to build an IKEv2 connection with PSK auth and a tunnel-mode child SA (local_ts/remote_ts = 10.10.10.0/24 <-> 10.20.20.0/24) on both firewalls.

Generated a random PSK on node1 and applied the identical value on both firewalls (passed only via secret_env, never printed). Enabled the legacy ipsec.enable flag and ran configctl ipsec reload on both nodes.

Configured static private addressing and routes on node3 (10.10.10.10/24 on enp8s0, route to 10.20.20.0/24 via 10.10.10.1) and node4 (10.20.20.10/24 on enp8s0, route to 10.10.10.0/24 via 10.20.20.1), persisted via NetworkManager connection profiles so they survive reboot.
Verified pre-tunnel baseline: node3 could not reach node4's private IP (isolated networks, as required).

Verified post-tunnel: swanctl -l shows ESTABLISHED IKE_SA and INSTALLED tunnel-mode CHILD_SA on both firewalls; node3 pings node4 successfully over private addresses; tcpdump on the transit interface shows only ESP packets (no plaintext), confirming encryption in transit.

Captured pre-restart boot-identity baselines for all 4 nodes (kern.boottime for node1/node2, /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id for node3/node4) plus healthy-state proof (established IPsec SAs, working pings).

Restarted node1 via 'shutdown -r now' (backgrounded so ack returned before disconnect); polled until exec available; confirmed kern.boottime changed; verified IPsec re-established, interfaces reconfigured, pf active, and node3->node4 ping succeeded.
Restarted node2 the same way; confirmed kern.boottime changed; verified IPsec re-established and node4->node3 ping succeeded.
Restarted node3 via 'systemctl reboot'; confirmed boot_id changed; verified private IP/route persisted via NetworkManager and node3->node4 ping succeeded.
Restarted node4 via 'systemctl reboot'; confirmed boot_id changed; verified private IP/route persisted and node4->node3 ping succeeded.
Final full-system verification: both firewalls show ESTABLISHED/INSTALLED IPsec SAs and bidirectional private-address connectivity confirmed after all four restarts.
Cleaned up temporary scripts and config.xml backup files created during the session.

evidence.requirement: IPsec tunnel established between node1 and node2 carrying private networks lan-a/lan-b
evidence.summary: swanctl -l on node1 and node2 shows ESTABLISHED IKEv2 SA and INSTALLED TUNNEL CHILD_SA with local/remote traffic selectors 10.10.10.0/24 <-> 10.20.20.0/24

evidence.requirement: node3 and node4 reach each other by private addresses
evidence.summary: Successful ping from node3 (10.10.10.10) to node4 (10.20.20.10) and back over private IPs, both immediately after tunnel setup and after all node restarts
tcpdump on node1's vtnet1 (transit interface) while node3 pings node4 shows only ESP packets between 10.99.99.1 and 10.99.99.2, no plaintext ICMP

evidence.requirement: Private networks isolated before tunnel (baseline falsification)
evidence.summary: Ping from node3 to node4's private IP fails (100% loss) before IPsec was configured, confirming networks were genuinely isolated

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: kern.boottime baseline 16:50:59; reboot acknowledged; kern.boottime changed to 17:01:42; swanctl shows re-established SA and node3->node4 ping succeeds post-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: kern.boottime baseline 16:50:59; reboot acknowledged; kern.boottime changed to 17:02:19; swanctl shows re-established SA and node4->node3 ping succeeds post-restart

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id baseline 5b620f5a...; reboot issued via systemctl reboot; boot_id changed to 0c257b95...; private IP/route persisted and node3->node4 ping succeeds post-restart

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id baseline 2c237d4f...; reboot issued via systemctl reboot; boot_id changed to 251e8f47...; private IP/route persisted and node4->node3 ping succeeds post-restart

evidence.requirement: Final full-cluster health after all restarts
evidence.summary: Both firewalls show ESTABLISHED IKE_SA/INSTALLED CHILD_SA and bidirectional node3<->node4 pings succeed after all four node restarts completed
